---
type: choice
title: 'A negative of a negative, $-(-2)$'
---

Which statement is **true**?

- [x] $-(-2) < 10$
- [ ] $-(-2) > 10$
- [ ] $-(-2) = -2$
- [ ] $-(-2) < -10$

## Hint
Work out $-(-2)$ first, then compare the result with $10$ or $-10$.

## Hint
$-a$ means "the opposite of $a$". What is the opposite of $-2$?

## Solution
**Answer:** $-(-2) < 10$

The opposite of $-2$ is $2$, so $-(-2) = 2$. Then $2 < 10$ is true.

- **$-(-2) = -2$**: this ignores one of the two minus signs. Two minus signs cancel: $-(-2) = 2$.
- **$-(-2) < -10$**: this would mean $2 < -10$, but every positive number is greater than every negative number.
- **$-(-2) > 10$**: this would mean $2 > 10$, which is false.
